title: Eclipses
examples: What is the difference between a solar and a lunar eclipse?
Why can't I look at the sun during an eclipse?
What causes the Earth to block the sun's light?

explain.say: Today we learn about eclipses in space.
A solar eclipse happens when the moon blocks the sun's light.
A lunar eclipse happens when the earth blocks the sun's light.
All eclipses happen because three bodies line up in a straight line.
Never look directly at the sun during any eclipse event.

draw.text: Safety: Never look at the Sun

explain.say: When you are playing with flashlights in a dark room, it shows alignment.

faq.q: What is the difference between a solar and a lunar eclipse?
faq.a: In a solar eclipse, the moon passes between the sun and earth. In a lunar eclipse, the earth passes between the sun and the moon.
asks: When is the moon in front of the sun?
Does the earth block the sun for a moon eclipse?

faq.q: Why do eclipses only happen sometimes?
faq.a: Eclipses require the sun, earth, and moon to line up perfectly. This perfect alignment does not happen every single month.
asks: Do the planets always line up?

faq.q: Is it safe to look at the sun even during an eclipse?
faq.a: No, it is very dangerous to look at the sun without special protection. You must always wear certified eclipse glasses.
asks: Can regular glasses protect my eyes?
What should I do if I look at the sun?

faq.q: What is the order of the objects during a solar eclipse?
faq.a: The order is the sun, then the moon, and finally the earth. The moon is blocking the sun's light.
asks: What is in the middle of a solar eclipse?
Which object is in front of the sun?

faq.q: What causes the moon to appear in the path?
faq.a: The moon orbits the earth, and sometimes its path crosses the line between the sun and earth. This causes the eclipse.
asks: Does the moon orbit the sun?
Why does the moon pass through?

facts: A solar eclipse occurs when the moon passes between the sun and earth.
A lunar eclipse occurs when the earth passes between the sun and the moon.
It is never safe to look directly at the sun's surface.
All eclipses depend on the three bodies lining up in sequence.

quiz.say: If the Earth is between the Sun and Moon, what type of eclipse happens?
quiz.why: The earth blocks the sun's light for the moon, causing a lunar eclipse.

wrong.0: The earth is definitely blocking the light in this setup.
wrong.1: The setup describes only one specific type of eclipse.
wrong.3: This happens when the moon blocks the sun, not the earth.

quiz.say: What must you use to safely view a total solar eclipse?
quiz.why: These glasses filter the sun's bright rays to keep your eyes safe.

wrong.0: You must look at the area safely, not just look away.
wrong.1: Cardboard boxes do not block the sun's intense light completely.
wrong.3: Regular sunglasses do not block enough of the sun's harmful rays.

quiz.say: For a solar eclipse, what is the correct order of the three bodies?
quiz.why: The moon must pass between the sun and earth for the shadow to fall on earth.

wrong.0: This arrangement does not block the sun's light effectively.
wrong.2: This order would create a lunar eclipse, not a solar one.
wrong.3: The moon cannot be in front of the sun like that to cause an eclipse.
